beginner.rationale: Beginners read fewer position changes and no wide stretches more easily (verification spec goals row "Be easy to play"; literature 4.2); the multipliers scale the learned penalties rather than replacing them, so the model's knowledge of idiomatic fingerings is kept, and fiveOnBlack keeps the fifth off black keys (teacher review criterion beginner_friendly). A thumb crossing inside one five-finger position (lint L15) is what a teacher crosses out on a level 1 or 2 piece (docs/reviews/ui-2026-10-14.md, Twinkle bars 3-4), a crossing of two fingers without the thumb (L06) is an error for a beginner anywhere, and a fast hop (L11) breaks the legato: the level adds a fixed cost to every pair of notes lint --beginner flags with one of them, since the learned transition indicators reward crossings and a multiplier may not touch them.
beginner.note: M3 Task 8, fix round 2, measured with learned-open on the 22 library pieces of level 1 to 3 (15 of level 1 and 2), hand profiles medium and large, and on the textbook oracle; numbers read expert to beginner, medium / large. Lint costs. L15, L06 and L11 cost 30 each. The first version charged thumb crossings inside a position alone: L15 went to 0, but the decode put two other fingers over each other or one finger on two keys instead; on the level 1 and 2 pieces the lint --beginner errors (all L06) rose from 2 to 5 and L11 from 2 to 4 on both hands (Pachelbel E5 2 then D5 5, a 3 over 4 in each minuet, La Candeur B4 1 then C5 1). With the three costs, level 1 and 2: errors 2 to 0 / 2 to 0, L11 2 to 0 / 2 to 0, L15 12 to 0 / 13 to 0, position changes 384 to 352 / 375 to 341; level 1 to 3: errors 59 to 48 / 46 to 41, L06 15 to 4 / 9 to 4, L11 4 to 0 / 4 to 0, L15 17 to 1 / 18 to 1 (Pastorale), position changes 1170 to 1110 / 1143 to 1092. No piece has more errors or fast hops than at the expert level. Any equal cost from 17 to 60 gives the same lint and position-change counts on these pieces; 15 leaves 1 L15 on the level 1 and 2 pieces and 12 leaves 2 L15 and 2 L11, so 30 keeps a margin. The costs are equal on purpose: L06 at 60 with the others at 30 brings back 2 L15 on Pachelbel's Canon. L06 is not charged after a rest (the hand is lifted there; lint still reports it): charged, it made Burgmuller's Arabesque move the left hand once more (43 to 44) to avoid a 4 then 5 across a rest. Position changes: no piece more on the medium hand; on the large hand La Candeur 45 to 46, Pastorale 61 to 62 and Innocence 44 to 45, every other piece the same or fewer. Multipliers. handPositionShift and stretch are needed with the costs: back at 1, Pachelbel keeps 2 L15 and the position changes rise (1170 to 1173 / 1143 to 1152). handPositionShift above 1.5 loses exact scales (first version: 1.6: 4, 1.75: 8, 2: 10). The plan's list also scaled positionChangeSize, largeSpan, thumbOnBlack and sameFingerPivot by 1.5; positionChangeSize, largeSpan and sameFingerPivot stay at 1 (first version, alone on the medium hand: positionChangeSize 1.5 moved the hand anchor more often on 8 pieces and lost 2 exact scales, 1.25 with the other multipliers lost 8; largeSpan 1.5 lost 4 exact scales; sameFingerPivot 1.5 moved the anchor more often on 2 pieces). fiveOnBlack 3 (not in the plan's list) keeps the fifth off black keys: L09 level 1 and 2 2 to 2 / 2 to 2, level 1 to 3 10 to 7 / 14 to 13; at 1 the level gave 5 / 7 and 15 / 26, at 2 5 / 3 and 17 / 18, and 4 adds position changes on Clementi and the C major Prelude. thumbOnBlack stays at 1, a recorded trade: the level puts the thumb on a black key (L08) where it removes a crossing or a hop, level 1 and 2 4 to 11 / 3 to 8, level 1 to 3 9 to 21 / 7 to 13 (Pachelbel, both minuets, La Candeur on the medium hand, Pastorale, Clementi; profilesWeights.test.ts pins L08 + L09 per piece). thumbOnBlack 1.25 brings back 2 L15 on Pachelbel's Canon on the medium hand, 1.5 and 2 on both hands. A cost on L08 itself, tried before the rest exception at 1.5 to 10 with the other costs at 20, left 3 or 4 L15 on the level 1 and 2 pieces, and 1 with L15 at 100; the consistent-repeats pass then picks for the canon's repeated bars a fingering with a crossing inside a position (without the pass, those bars have none). Stretches. The level changes no stretch wider than an octave (wideStretches), on either hand. No piece holds keys more than an octave apart on the medium hand at either level, a property of the scores (Satie holds 7 such pairs on the large hand at both levels), and the 5 legato reaches of 13 and 14 semitones the expert fingering makes on the medium hand stay (Bach's G minor minuet, Schumann's Melody twice, the C major Prelude's left hand twice): stretch 1.5 prices a reach within the practical span too little to turn it into a hand shift. Textbook. The lint costs lose no textbook entry (alone: none lost, Db major RH down 3 octaves gained). One- and two-octave scales 280 of 288 exact at both levels on both hands (8 endings of F harmonic minor RH and F# melodic minor LH are not exact at the expert level either), chromatic 48 of 48: a window of more than five distinct keys is no five-finger position (pairWindows). Known losses: arpeggios 170 of 192 at the expert level, 168 (medium) and 166 (large) at the beginner level, which starts Bb major and minor LH down on 2 instead of 3 and, on the large hand, changes one end of Eb dominant seventh LH up and down; the handPositionShift and stretch multipliers lose them (each back at 1 alone still loses the Bb arpeggios, both back at 1 keep them). Three-octave scales 103 to 104 of 144 (Db major RH down gained). Multipliers scale positive weights only: learned-open's positionChangeCount is negative and stays as it is.

expert.rationale: The weight set as it is.
